newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, September 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, September 26.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Communist Refoundation Party insists it is not going to accept any proposed cut in pensions and healthcare in the 1997 budget. Prime minister Romano Prodi is sure there will be no government crisis. The budget is due to be presented to the Council of Ministers on Friday 28 (all).

* Giorgio Fossa chairman of employers' association Confindustria says in an interview "We don't care which political majority will approve the 1997 budget. We do care that this government will bring us into Europe" (La Repubblica).

* Justice Minister Giovanni Maria Flick proposes measures to guarantee people's privacy when wire-tapping is used by magistrates to conduct an inquiry. Magistrates who leak to the press about undergoing inquiries will be punished (all).
* The 1997 budget is expected to contain 38.5 trillion lire of deficit cutting measures. An extra 22 trillion lire might be collected in 1997 with a special "tax for Europe" (all).
* International Monetary Fund said Italy will eventually join Emu, but cuts in pensions and healthcare are needed (all).
*Italian state telecoms holding Stet, due to be privatised in early 1997, posted a 12 pct rise in its first half pretax profit, hitting 4.04 trillion lire (all).
* The mark/lira cross went under 1,000 while fixed rate government bonds Btps are hitting new highs. (all)
* EU commissioner Karel Van Miert is cautious over public subsidies to financially troubled Banco di Napoli. "We are being very wary. In this case you might have some bad surprises" (Sole 24 ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
